key_insight: Update-Matched Unlearning (UMU) preserves a model’s ability to learn new tasks while still blocking relearning of removed knowledge by matching the reference to the same post-unlearning update.
engineering_relevance: For deployed LLMs that keep getting fine-tuned, UMU offers a practical way to maintain plasticity after unlearning instead of accidentally freezing future adaptation.
method: Apply the same simulated relearning update to both the defended model and an undefended reference initialized from the same unlearned checkpoint.
Use an update-matched reference rather than a pre-update reference when judging how much the model should change after an update.
Select the defended model using new-task learning performance so suppression does not come at the cost of plasticity.
evidence_signal: Across TOFU and FaithUn with Llama and Qwen models, UMU improved relearning resistance and plasticity, reducing harmful and benign relearning by 30.4 and 9.9 points on average while increasing new-task accuracy by 3.5 points.
watch_item: The benefit depends on how well the simulated update matches the real downstream fine-tuning process, so mismatched update assumptions could weaken the defense.
paper_title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
